definitions: A theory in fluid dynamics that describes the motion of fluids in terms of vortices.
A historical theory in physics that attempted to explain the structure of matter and the universe through the properties of vortices in an ethereal fluid.
examples: Early attempts to understand turbulence often involved vortex theory.
Descartes' cosmology was an elaborate vortex theory.
Modern aerodynamics heavily relies on principles derived from vortex theory.
